He was not concerned with the fear of God—even though he offered sacrifices as a hypocrite <note>original: "Gleißner"; a term for a religious hypocrite who makes a "glistering" or shining outward show of piety while remaining corrupt within.</note>—but rather with the region <note>original: "Region"; here meaning worldly territory, dominion, or political rank.</note>.

<margin>83. The Beginning of the Antichristian Kingdom.</margin>
And here the Antichristian kingdom begins: where one gives good words before God, yet the heart is possessed by greed <note>original: "Geiz"; in Böhme's time, this implied a broad sense of avarice or a grasping, selfish desire for power.</note>, and one strives only for might and power to rule over the wretched who trust in God. Therefore, the Antichrist has his god in a chest <note>A critique of institutional religion that traps God in material objects or rigid dogmas rather than living spirit.</note> and in the strength of his power, and a fox hangs from his coat <note>A traditional metaphor for cunning, deceit, and hidden predatory nature.</note>. He prays, but he only desires from God the kingdom of this world; his heart does not cease from being the driver and hunter of poor Abel. But Abel prays to the Lord, and his heart joins itself to the love of God, into the true image <note>original: "Bildniß"; refers to the "Image of God" in humanity, which Böhme believed was the spiritual goal of the Christian life to restore.</note>: for he desires the kingdom of heaven, and God’s blessing here for his nourishment.

<margin>84.</margin>
Now the devil cannot endure that a holy church should grow in his land. He always wants to murder Abel. As it then happened there: because Cain did not fear God, the devil gained access to him and awakened the innate wrath <note>original: "Grim"; refers to the "Grimmigkeit" or the dark, fiery quality of the first principle of nature which, when unbalanced by light, leads to violence.</note> in Cain against Abel, so that he struck him dead.

Then all the devils must surely have danced and thought: "Now the kingdom is ours once more." Because of this, Adam and Eve were terrified when they saw that the one whom they held to be a prince became a murderer: and as the history relates, they did not engage in procreation <note>original: "Vermiſchung"; literally "mixing," a common euphemism for sexual intercourse.</note> for seventy years.

Do you ask why? See, I will tell you: You are Cain, the lord of this world, for you have made yourself such. Thus Abel is now your servant; he entered this world as a guest. But he rises again and brings forth out of this world back into his Fatherland. You cannot endure him; you press him to the ground in two ways, all quite cunningly and in your own power. First, with your hypocritical, false teaching at <term>Babel</term><note>In Böhme’s terminology, "Babel" represents the confusion of institutionalized, "man-made" religion that lacks the living Spirit of God.</note>, in which he must and shall believe what you prescribe for him without God’s Spirit. With this, you pull him on a path away from God into the spirit of this world, so that he must look to your chatter; and if he does not do that, you murder him along with Abel.

<margin>110.</margin>

<margin>111.</margin>

<summary>Böhme uses the biblical figures of Cain and Abel to describe the internal and social oppression of the godly spirit by worldly power and religious hypocrisy. He critiques both the physical bondage of serfdom and the spiritual bondage of "Babel," or corrupt institutional religion.</summary>

Each one thinks his way is the right one and that he walks on the proper path. He is always murdered in two ways.

<margin>Chapter 21.</margin>
...a false, evil, and devilish one, wherein one perceives **Divine Providence** <note>original: "Göttliche Fürsichtigkeit"; refers to God's foresight and governing care over the world.</note> in all things, and yet also the Devil’s deceit, cunning, and malice in all things.

<margin>1.</margin>
In Divine Providence, we find in all things—in all arts and stations of life—that the essences of this world are all good and useful; it is only the poison sown within them by the Devil that is evil.

We also find that all stations, both high and low, arise from a single source, and one proceeds from the other, so that Divine Providence comes to the aid of all things. Thus, the eternal wonders in all <term>three principles</term> <note>Böhme’s foundational system: the dark fire-source, the light of divine love, and the visible world of nature.</note> are revealed. To this end, God brought the creation of all things into the light; from eternity, these things existed within themselves only in <term>laboring quality</term> <note>original: "Qualen"; a central Böhme term playing on the words for "torment" and "source/quelling." <margin>2.</margin>

When the Divine Law judged him to death in his conscience, the Divine Answer spoke against it: "No, whoever slays Cain shall be avenged sevenfold." With this decree, the fierce avenger—the abyss of hell—was driven away from him, so that Cain would not despair; and although he had truly gone out from God, the kingdom of heaven still stood open to him, that he might turn back and [enter] into

# 449 Of the Divine Being

<margin>Chapter 21.</margin>
...they still are: and the struggle remains for eternity, for it is also from eternity. As 1. **Wrath** <term>Wrath</term> <note>original: "Grimm"; in Böhme’s theology, this refers to the fiery, harsh, and active quality of the divine foundation that provides energy and movement.</note>, and 2. **Gentleness** <term>Gentleness</term> <note>original: "Sanfftmuht"; the light-filled, loving, and peaceful quality that balances the divine Wrath.</note> (for if there were no wrath, there would also be no movement in eternity. 13. ### Of the Kingdom of Christ in this World.

39. **B**ecause man had then truly entered this world in the spirit, and now possessed all the gates within—such as the kingdom of heaven, as well as the kingdom of hell and also the kingdom of this world—he therefore had to live in the "press" <note>original: "quätsche" — a crushing squeeze or pressure between two opposing forces</note> between heaven and this world. There, the devil awakened one mocker after another, who raised up the kingdom of wrath <term>Grimmigkeit</term> <note>A central term in Böhme’s thought, referring to the harsh, fire-like, and vengeful aspect of nature when it is not tempered by divine light and love.</note> and constantly stirred up conflict against the children of God. Thus the world became full of tyrants, as well as bestial violators of blood, murderers, and thieves, because greed had grown. Therefore, the office of the ruler was most useful, so that it might restrain the godless oppressor with force.

40. And one sees how Divine Providence <term>Fürsichtigkeit</term> itself comes to the aid of the kingdom of this world, and through the spirit of this world awakens rulers who carried out punishment. But the Spirit of God complains about them, that they have become tyrants who suppressed everything under them with force. And now Abel’s church <note>In Böhme’s typology, Abel represents the true, humble, and spiritual believer, whereas Cain represents the worldly and institutionalized power.</note> would not consist therein in love, but rather the strong power of God was used to suppress the evildoer.

41. Indeed, the judges and kings, as well as princes and governors, are God's officials in the house of this world, whom God has appointed because of sin, so that they should "cut sharply" <note>meaning to exercise strict justice or the power of the sword</note> so that the oppressor of the godless might be restrained.

42. And their station is founded in the original source <term>Uhrkundt</term> <note>Böhme uses this term to refer to the fundamental "original record" or essential foundation of all existence.</note> of beings, for in the beginning God created the thrones according to His eternal wisdom; just as there are throne-princes in heaven, so also there are such in hell, and thus in regions according to the seven spirits of eternal nature.

<summary>Böhme explains the divine necessity of secular government and rulers as a consequence of human sin and the "wrath" of the world. He argues that while kings and judges are God's officials meant to restrain evil, they frequently succumb to the temptation of becoming tyrants.</summary>

The Father’s **essences** <term>essences (original: *Essentien*); in Böhme's cosmogony, these are the active, underlying qualities or "driving forces" of divine being</term>, as he enters into himself through the eternal gates—as described in Chapter 22—within the eternal mind through the recaptured will, into the eternal joy forever and ever, where he generates his eternal Word.

<margin>Chapter 22.</margin> [He] was conceived and born of a pure Virgin, without sin.

<margin>30. 1 Cor. 2:14</margin>

<margin>31. Luke 1:28</margin>

Before heaven and earth were created, she was a Virgin, and moreover entirely pure, without any blemish. And this same pure, chaste Virgin of God entered into Mary during her incarnation and was her **New Man** <note>The spiritual, reborn nature of the believer</note> in the holy element of God. This is the second **Principle** <term>Principle (original: *Principium*); one of the three fundamental realities in Böhme's cosmos: 1. The Father's Fire, 2. The Son's Light/Paradise, 3. The physical world</term>. This same [Principle] exists within all things, yet the thing itself—being a dead, dark **outgrowth** <term>outgrowth (original: *Ausgebuhrt*); the external, physical manifestation of spiritual forces</term>—does not know it, just as the pot does not know the potter; nor can the thing seize or grasp it. For when I lift or grasp something, I cannot say that I am grasping the holy element, Paradise, or the Godhead. Rather, I grasp the **outgrowth**, the kingdom of this world, which is the third **Principle** and its essence, and I do not move the Godhead by doing so. Thus, we are to recognize the Holy **New Man** hidden within the **Old Man**, and yet they are not separated until the death of the body.

# Of the Divine Essence

<margin>Chapter 22</margin>
...[the earthly] element does not grasp [the divine], just as little as the body grasps the soul. Likewise, *Christ* truly took our human essences <term>essences: the fundamental properties or "substance" of human nature</term> upon himself in the body of the Virgin *Mary* and became our brother. Yet these human essences cannot grasp his eternal Godhead; only the new man born in God grasps the Godhead, in the same way that the body relates to the soul, and in no other way.

<margin>42.</margin>
Therefore, the body of *Christ* is beneath the Godhead, and within these our human essences, he suffered death. His Godhead went into death in the midst of the holy man within the pure element <note>The "pure element" refers to the spiritual world or the "quintessence" that exists behind the four physical elements.</note>, and took away death’s power. He separated the natural soul—which *Christ* commended to his Father as he died on the Cross—from the kingdom of this world, as well as from death, the devil, and hell, through his mighty Divine power. He opened a gate for all of us who come to him and claim him as our own with our senses and minds. In this way, the Father draws our soul, which is in him, into the pure love of *Christ*. There, the soul sets its imagination <term>imagination: in Böhme’s thought, this refers to the soul’s power of focus and desire that shapes its inner reality</term> once again through *Christ* into the Holy Trinity. It is then fed by the Word of the Lord <note>original: "Verbo Domini"</note>, where it becomes an angel once again, purely separated from the kingdom of the devil and this world through the death of *Christ*.

<margin>43.</margin>

It was not at all for the sake of the animal body, which must melt back into the four elements and become nothing; of which nothing remains but the shadow in the figure of all the works and beings that it ever made.

Thus God is a spirit, and the pure Element is heavenly earth, for it is substantial; and the essences in the heavenly earth are the Paradise of growth; and the Virgin of Wisdom is to be compared thus to the great spirit of the entire heavenly world; and she reveals the great wonders not only in the heavenly earth, but also in the entire depth of the Godhead.

<margin>63.</margin>
For the Godhead is incomprehensible and invisible, yet perceptible; but the Virgin is visible as a pure spirit, and the Element is her body; this is called the *Holy Ternary* <note>original: "Ternarius Sanctus"</note>, the holy earth.

And into this *Holy Ternary* the invisible Godhead has entered, so that it may be an eternal marriage; so that, to speak in an analogy, the Godhead is in the pure Element, and the Element is the Godhead. For God and the *Holy Ternary* have become one thing—not in spirit, but in essence—just like body and soul; and as the soul is over the body, so also is God over the *Holy Ternary*.

79. + O you blind wolves of Babel, what have we to do with you? For we are not born of your kingdom; why do you want to tear our dear Immanuel out of our eyes and hearts, and want to make us blind? # Of the Three Principles

<margin>Chapter 23.</margin> [The] birth of his body <note>Referring to the spiritual or heavenly body of Christ/the New Man.</note> / we recognize four things: **Fire**, **Air**, **Water**, and **Earth**, within which our [earthly] body stands.

So also, within the **Heavenly Body**, there are likewise four things: The **Fire** is the kindling of the **Desire**; the **Water** is that which the Fire desires, by which the Fire becomes soft and gentle; the **Air** is the joyful Spirit which blows upon the Fire and creates movement within the Water; and the **Earth** is truly the **Essence** <note>The spiritual substance or "beingness."</note> which is born out of the [other] three, and is rightly called *Terra Sanctus* <note>original: "Terra Sanctus"; Holy Earth.</note>, in which the **Tincture** <note>In alchemy and Böhme's thought, the Tincture is the transformative spiritual "dye" or life-force that brings perfection to matter.</note> is born, as the quality of **Gentleness**, within which the holy blood and water are born as an oil of the water, in which the light shines and the Spirit of God stands.

24. Thus understand, the **Water of Eternal Life** is within the **Limbus of God** <note>original: "Limbo Gottes"; the spiritual "soil" or matrix of divine potential.</note>, in the *Ternario Sancto* <note>original: "Ternario Sancto"; the Holy Ternary or the manifestation of the Trinity in a substantial, spiritual state.</note>, and it is the water which baptizes the soul, provided they remain in the practice of His testament. For the soul, within Christ’s covenant, is dipped and washed in that same water, and it is truly a new **rebirth** <margin>Titus 3:5.</margin> <note>Referring to the "washing of regeneration" mentioned in the Epistle to Titus.</note>. For the soul is received and refreshed by the Holy Spirit within the holy water, and by the holy water itself; it enters into the covenant of Christ—into the soul of Christ, though not *into* it directly, but rather into His **body**, and thus becomes Christ’s **soul-brother**. For Christ’s soul is a creature just like our soul, and it is surrounded by the **Tincture** within the Body of Mercy, possessing it within itself as food and strength. # A Beautiful Mirror for All Hungry, Penitent Souls.
<margin>Chapter 24.</margin>

<margin>1.</margin>
My dear reader! We declare this to you: that all things, proceeding from the <term>original source</term> <note>original: "Uhrkunde." Böhme uses this term to describe the primordial origin or "primal record" of all being.</note> of the <term>Essence of all essences</term> <note>original: "Wesen aller Wesen." A common Böhmean term for the Ground of all being or the Godhead.</note>, each have their impulse in their own form according to their origin; and that thing always creates the same essence with which the spirit is pregnant. The body must always work within that in which the spirit is kindled. When I reflect and consider why I write in this way, rather than leaving it to other clever and sharp-minded people, I find that my spirit is kindled in this essence about which I write. For there is a living, running fire of these things in my spirit. Therefore, whatever else I undertake, this matter always wells up from within, and thus I am captured by it in my spirit; it is laid upon me as a work that I must perform. Since it is then my work, which my spirit pursues, I will write it down as a <term>Memorial</term> <note>A remembrance or written record intended to preserve a spiritual experience for the future.</note> for myself—and in exactly such a manner as I recognize it in my spirit, and in the way I came to it. I will set down nothing foreign, nothing that I have not experienced myself, so that I may not be found a liar before God.

<margin>2.</margin>
If it should happen that someone desires to follow after me and craves the knowledge of these things about which I write, I give him this advice: that he should follow me in the <term>Table of Succession</term> <note>original: "Nachfolge-Taffel." This refers to the progression of Böhme's arguments or the spiritual path he maps out in the text.</note>, not immediately with the pen, but rather with the labor of the <term>mind</term> <note>original: "Gemüht." In Böhme's terminology, the *Gemüht* is the seat of the soul's desires, will, and emotional disposition; it is the "inner man."</note>. Then he will experience how I have been able to write thus, even though I have not been taught by the schools of this world—except only a very little—with this meager <term>handwriting</term> <note>original: "Handschrifft." Böhme refers to his own lack of formal academic training, identifying himself as a simple craftsman rather than a scholar.</note> which is before your eyes.

Therefore, the world never stays in one order from one time to the next; people considered them fools, and the same happens to you. After you are gone, things will remain as they ever were. What then does your great sorrow and toil avail you?"

# The Gate of the Poor Sinner.

Therefore, you dear soul, if you have indeed fallen into blasphemy and heavy sin through the deception of the *Antichrist* <term>Antichrist <note>In Böhme’s theology, this is not just a single historical figure, but a spirit of pride and false teaching that inhabits corrupt religious and political systems.</note></term> and the temptation of the Devil and his followers, bethink yourself quickly. For we could never have escaped from this evil eternally if the mercy of God had not helped us out, without our own knowledge or merit.

### Chapter 25. Mobility, the Kingdom, Power and Glory

And immediately life blossomed through death; there death was broken and became a mockery. To the godless, who remained in the Wrath, it is a death; but to the Saints in Christ, it is a Life.

<margin>73+</margin> Thus the soul of Christ rested forty hours in the Grave in the Father, present with its body.

Von den drey Principien <note>original: "Of the Three Principles" — the title of Böhme's 1619 work exploring the nature of God and the universe through three foundational modes of existence.</note>

<margin>Chapter 25.</margin>
### Of Christ’s Ascension.

98. Thus we know, that just as Adam had lived forty days in Paradise, he entered into the spirit of this world at the moment he should have entered into the Holy Trinity; he stood in the time of temptation, and if he had withstood those forty days, he would have stood fully with his soul in the Light of God, and in his *Holy Ternary* <note>original: "Ternario Sancto" — a term Böhme uses to describe the divine, spiritual corporeality or the manifestation of the Trinity in a person</note>, as this Christ did.

99. For after Christ had walked forty days in this world after his resurrection as a *proof* <note>original: "proba" — a test or evidence of his victory over death</note>, he went up onto a mountain, to which he summoned his <margin>Acts 1:9.</margin> disciples, and ascended visibly into the heights in his own body—the very body he had offered up on the cross—until a cloud came and hid him from their sight. This was a certain sign that he was their brother and that he had not <margin>Matthew 28:20.</margin> left them in this earthly form and body; just as he then also said to them: "Lo, I am with you always, even unto the end of the world."

100. Now Reason speaks: Where has Christ gone? Has he gone out of this world, high above the stars into another heaven? Hear, my dear Reason, incline your mind toward Christ, and see; I will tell you, for we see and know it—not I. For when I speak as "We," you must not understand merely my earthly humanity; for the Spirit that drives this pen is also named with me: Therefore I write and say, when I wish to speak of myself as the author, "We." For I knew nothing, if the Spirit had not breathed knowledge into me; and it could not have been found in any other way, for the Spirit did not wish it otherwise, but rather hid itself until my soul showed itself quite restless within me with great longing for the Spirit, until I learned what it was.

<meta>catchword: Therefore</meta>

<margin>Chapter 25.</margin>
101. See, this is not the foundation that has been imagined and measured by the ancients, who calculated how many hundred thousand miles it might be to the heaven where Christ ascended? They did this for the purpose of wanting to be God on Earth, as their imagined kingdom shows, which stands more in Babel <note>Böhme uses "Babel" to represent the confusion and pride of man-made religious systems.</note>. When we speak of the thrones, it is much different, and here one finds their blindness and ignorance. Although in their knowledge there is also a spirit that one should not simply cast aside, it is not from the *Holy Ternary* <note>original: "Ternario Sancto"; Böhme's term for the divine spiritual manifestation or the "body" of the Trinity.</note>, not from the body of Jesus Christ, but from the high eternity that moves above the thrones, of which more can be mentioned in another place.

<margin>102.</margin>
We must remain in our own throne; what do the other thrones concern me, which belong to the princely angels? They are, nonetheless, our friends and dear faithful ones in the service of God (Hebrews 1:4). We must look toward our own throne, in which we were created as creatures, and toward our princely leader <note>original: "Thron-fürsten"; refers to Christ as the head of the human spiritual realm.</note> in God. The first purpose of God, when He created us and saw us in the eternal bond, must stand firm.

<margin>103.</margin>
<margin>Throne of the second principle, in which God created humanity.</margin>
This throne belonged to Lucifer with his legions; but when he fell, he was cast out into the *first principle* <note>The first principle in Böhme's system is the source of nature, often associated with fire, darkness, and divine wrath.</note>. Thus the throne in the *second principle* <note>The second principle is the realm of light, love, and the divine heart.</note> stood empty, and therein God created humanity, who was intended to remain there; and man was tested to see if it were possible. Therefore God created the *third principle* <note>The third principle is the visible, material world.</note> in the place of this world, so that if humanity fell, they would not also become a devil, but might instead be helped and advised. Therefore, the enmity of the devil is directed against Christ, because Christ sits upon his [Lucifer's] royal throne, and the devil still holds man captive with his principle <note>The principle of wrath and darkness.</note>.

<summary>Böhme explains that Christ's ascension was not a physical journey to a distant heaven but an entry into a spiritual "throne" or dimension. He clarifies that humanity was created to occupy the spiritual realm vacated by Lucifer, and that the material world was created as a middle ground to allow for human redemption after the Fall.</summary>

# Of the Three Principles

<margin>Chapter 25.</margin>
<margin>104.</margin>
Therefore, the place <note>original: "locus"</note> of this world—according to the Heavenly Principle, our Christ—is his throne and his own body. Everything that exists in this world within the third principle <note>The "third principle" refers to the visible, material world of nature and the four elements.</note> is his own. Even the devil, who dwells in this same place but within the first principle <note>The "first principle" is the dark, fiery source of strength and wrath that exists behind all manifestation.</note>, is a prisoner of our Christ.

<margin>105.</margin>
For all thrones are within God the Father, and outside of Him there is nothing. He is the bond of eternity. However, His love—dwelling in the body of Christ as if in its own throne—holds the wrath within the bond of eternity captive, along with the devils. You must understand how everything has the nature of a creature <note>original: "Creatürlich"; meaning everything has a defined, created form and limit.</note>: His love and His wrath alike. There is only one birth <note>original: "Gebuhrt"; Böhme uses this to mean the process by which reality is continuously generated or "born."</note>, as was mentioned before. The distinction is such that one cannot say the devils live far away from Christ. No, they are near, but they are not reached by eternity. For they cannot see the clear Godhead in the light, but are blinded by it. In the same way, we would never see or feel them in eternity—just as we do not see them now—because they are in a different principle. Thus, that principle remains separate.

<margin>106.</margin>
Therefore, my dear soul <note>original: "Gemühte"; refers to the mind, spirit, or inner disposition of the reader.</note>, know that the creature of Christ is the center <note>original: "Centrum"</note> of this throne, from which all life (meaning heavenly life) goes out. For the Holy Trinity is in that center—and not only in that center, but in all angelic thrones, and also in the holy souls of human beings. We must speak in this way only so that you may understand.

So the body—meaning the creature, the man Christ—is seated in the midst of this throne. He stands thus in heaven (meaning in His own principle), sitting with His throne at the right hand of God the Father.

## Of the Various Sects and Contentions in Religion.

They even said—while being found evil and false themselves—that the Holy Spirit was powerful even in the mouth of the ungodly.

Then your light will shine in him, and you will awaken him from the death of sin and catch him with your love in your **tincture** <term>Tinktur; a spiritual life-force or medicinal quality that can transform the soul</term>; then he will come to you with heartfelt pleading and a desire for the Kingdom of Heaven. Then you are truly a **confessor** <note>original: "Beicht-Vater"</note> and you have **Peter’s keys**; but if you are outside of this, then you have no key.

<margin>26.</margin>
As the confession is, so also is the **absolution** <note>the formal release from guilt or sin</note>. If the patient is a **historicus** <term>Historicus; Böhme’s term for one who has intellectual knowledge of scripture but lacks living faith</term>, then so is the doctor; and in both there is a mouth-hypocrisy. But if the patient is powerful [in spirit], then the voice also blows upon power—not out of the power of the doctor, but in the power of God, who also makes growth happen with His power in a **thornbush** <note>original: "Dornpusche"</note> <margin><note>Handwritten checkmark-like symbol</note></margin> so that it turns green; which is the power in all beings, and thus also in a voice that has no power in itself.

<margin>27.</margin>
Thus it became the fashion that everyone was bound to the **stone temple** <note>the physical, institutional church building as opposed to the internal temple of the soul</note>, and the temple of God in Christ remained very much empty. But when they saw the desolation in the bickering, they established **councils** <note>original: "Concilia"; formal meetings of church leaders to decide on doctrine</note> and made laws that everyone should follow under penalty of losing one's life. Thus, from the temple of Christ a stone temple was made, and from the testimony of the Holy Spirit a worldly law; the Holy Spirit no longer spoke freely, but rather he was [expected to speak only through these laws].

<summary>Böhme argues that true spiritual authority and the "Keys of Peter" belong only to those who possess the Holy Spirit, contrasting living faith with the "mouth-hypocrisy" of institutional confession and worldly church laws.</summary>

<margin>4.</margin>
The Last Judgment is regarded in this way: just as we know how all things took their beginning, so shall they also have their end. For before the times of the world, there was nothing but the eternal band <term>Bande; the fundamental spiritual connection or knot of divine properties that precedes physical existence</term>, which made itself; and in the band was the Spirit, and the Spirit was in God, who is the highest Good, who ever was from eternity and never took a beginning. But this world has a beginning out of the eternal band within time.

<margin>5.</margin>
For this world creates a time; therefore it must pass away. And just as it was once a "nothing," so it will become a "nothing" again. For the Spirit hovered in the ether <note>original: "Æther"; the subtle spiritual atmosphere or heavenly element</note>, and within it was born the Limbo <note>original: "Limbus"; in Böhme’s thought, this refers to the transitional, formative substance or "chaos" from which physical matter was shaped</note>, which is transitory, and out of which all things come. At that time, there was no carver <note>original: "Schnizer"; a craftsman or sculptor</note> other than the Spirit in the essences <note>original: "Essentien"</note>, or the Vulcan <term>Vulcanus; a term borrowed from alchemy referring to the inner "fire-artist" or natural force that shapes and refines matter</term>. Furthermore, there were no essences unless they were born in the will of the Spirit; therein is the carver, who has carved all things out of nothing—simply out of the will. Since it is then carved out of the eternal will, it is eternal—not in its outward substance <note>original: "Wesen"</note>, but in the will. And after the breaking of the substance, this world stands entirely in the will, as a figure <note>original: "Figur"; a symbolic representation or permanent spiritual pattern</note> of God’s wondrous deeds.

<margin>6.</margin>
Thus we know that where a will exists, it must grasp itself so that it is a will; and this grasping creates an attraction, and that which is attracted is in the will,

1. Since in our previous writings there are several words which might be misunderstood by the reader, especially where we have written: we will be in the resurrection of the dead in the body of Jesus Christ in the <term>Holy Ternary; original Latin: "Ternario Sancto"</term>. While we have called the <term>Holy Ternary; original Latin: "Ternarium Sanctum"</term> "holy earth," it should not be understood as common soil, but rather as the holy body arising from the holy power of the <term>Trinity of God; original: "Dreyheit Gottes"</term>. In our writing, the "Holy Ternary" is actually understood as the gateways of God the Father, from whom all things proceed as if from a single essence.

Therefore, we wish to inform the reader of the second book of our writings somewhat more thoroughly, so that he does not merely cling to the bare letter and treat our writings as a <note>original: "Hiſtoriſch Weſen." Böhme warns against "historical" knowledge—meaning a literal or academic understanding that lacks personal spiritual experience.</note> historical matter; rather, he should pay attention to the sense and spirit—what is intended when the author speaks of the Divine Life. In these descriptions, the author does not use only one kind of word or name, even though sometimes three or four different names refer to exactly the same single life.

And yet the mind is such a wondrous being, and soon brings forth and raises another form out of one form—which just now was active or qualifying before all others—and <term>extinguishes; original: "verdämpffet," literally to dampen or smother a fire</term> the first ignited one, so that it is just like a nothingness, as is to be seen in joy and sorrow.

<meta>catchword: So</meta>

<summary>Böhme explains that all human emotions and actions, though contradictory, arise from a single source within the mind. He describes how different spiritual "forms" or qualities compete for dominance, with the leading quality determining a person's physical actions and emotional state.</summary>

If we now reflect upon the origin of all these things, we find primarily three forms in the <term>mind; original: "Gemühte," the seat of the soul's will and consciousness</term>. 1. We are not speaking only of the spirit of this world, for we find that our mind also has a longing for another mind, and it yearns for that which the eyes of the body do not see, and the mouth does not taste, and the touch of the earthly body does not grasp, nor the earthly hearing hear, nor the nose smell; but which the noble mind can see, taste, feel, grasp, and hear, provided the right Divine form is <note>original: "raͤhſch," an archaic term meaning dominant, active, or ruling</note> within it, or becomes <term>qualifying; original: "qualificirend," a technical term in Böhme’s thought meaning to operate or manifest according to a specific spiritual quality</term> above the other two forms. <margin>5.</margin>

Thereupon the third form immediately breaks forth out of the <note>original: "ewigen Bande," the "eternal bond" or the foundational, often harsh, structure of spiritual existence</note>, appearing as falsehood, envy, anger, and hatred; and thus the <term>image of God; original: "Bildnuͤß Gottes"</term> stands as if in death or overcome. Then the mind stands in the wrath of God, in death, and in the <term>jaws of hell; original: "Hoͤllen Rachen"</term>. In this, hell rejoices in the wrath of God, for its jaws are opened wide here and become active and qualifying. But when the Divine form breaks forth again, the kingdom of hell is overcome and becomes as if dead, and the kingdom of heaven becomes dominant and qualifying once more.

# Appendix.

...something, and yet in the **original source** <term>original: "Uhrkunde"; the primordial foundation or "first record" of an entity's existence.</term> there was nothing. And this same will goes out of itself within the **torment** <term>original: "Qual"; Böhme uses this word to denote both "torment/pain" and the "source-quality" (from *Quelle*, meaning wellspring) that drives all life.</term>, and creates for itself a freedom out of the torment; and the will desires that freedom, to stand within it, and it has its life from the will in the **light** <note>original: "Liechte"; the divine illumination that transforms the "fire" of the soul into "joy."</note>, and lives within itself in delight without torment, even though in its original source it stands in the ground of torment.

<margin>Hebrews 12:29; Deuteronomy 4:24 & 31</margin>
28. Therefore, my dear, precious, seeking **disposition** <term>original: "Gemühte"; the inner seat of the soul's will, thoughts, and emotions.</term>, know and observe that all life stands upon the abyss of **wrath** <term>original: "Grimm"; the fierce, severe, or "dark" side of God's nature that acts as the consuming fire of existence.</term>. For God also calls Himself a **consuming fire** <note>original: "verzehrend Fewr"; a reference to the divine justice and the energetic foundation of all being.</note>, and also a God of love; and His name "God" finds its original source in love, for He then goes out of the torment into Himself, and creates within Himself joy, Paradise, and the Kingdom of Heaven.

29. We all possess the torment of anger and wrath in the original source of our lives; otherwise, we would not be alive. But we must see to it that we, along with God, exit from the torment of the wrath within ourselves and bring forth love; then our life will become joy and lovely delight, and will stand rightly in the Paradise of God. But if our life remains in the wrath—such as in greed, envy, anger, and malice—and does not exit into another will, then it stands in the anxious torment just like all the devils, in whose life no good thought or will can exist, but rather a pure enmity within themselves.

30. Therefore, there are two lives: first, the life reborn in love; and second, the life in the original source of torment. These are set against one another; and as long as the life in love is not hostile, it must allow itself to be thus pricked by thorns and bruised, and the **cross** <note>The "cross" here represents the suffering and patience required to maintain a loving spirit in a harsh, "wrathful" world.</note> is laid upon it to be carried with the patience of gentleness. And a child of God must be a cross-bearer in this growth of this field: and to that...

<meta>catchword: end</meta>

<summary>Böhme describes the dual nature of existence, where life's "original source" is a consuming fire of wrath that must be transformed through the will into a life of love and joy. He argues that the "New Birth" requires turning away from selfish passions like greed and envy to experience the "Paradise" within.</summary>
<keywords>original source, torment, wrath, divine love, consuming fire, disposition, rebirth, the cross, spiritual growth</keywords>

# Appendix.

...[at the e]nd <note>The OCR begins mid-word; based on context, this is "Am Ende" (At the end).</note>, God has appointed a judgment and day of separation <term>original: "Scheide-tag"; refers to the Day of Judgment as a day of sorting or parting the good from the evil.</term> within himself, where he will harvest what has grown in every life; and all the forms of the eternal being will hereby become manifest, and everything must stand as God’s wondrous deeds.

<margin>31.</margin>
Therefore, O human! take heed, do not destroy yourself; see that you grow in the field of love, gentleness, and righteousness, and enter with your life within yourself into the gentleness of Jesus Christ, into the rebirth toward God; then you will live in God’s **torment of love** <term>original: "Qual der Liebe"; as noted previously, "Qual" implies both the "torment" of longing and the "source-quality" (Quelle) of life itself.</term>. And when the field of this growth is taken away from you, then your life will be a fruit and growth of God, and you will green and bloom with a new body out of the pure and holy element before God, in the life of your precious helper and redeemer Jesus Christ. To him, surrender yourself entirely in this **struggle-life** <note>original: "Streit-leben"; the earthly life characterized by the conflict between light and darkness, or spirit and flesh.</note>; then you will green with him through his death and resurrection as a new human before God.

->F I A T<-
<note>Latin: "Let it be done."</note>
->Amen!<-

<margin>28. Hebrews 12. 29. Deuteronomy 4. v. 4. & 31.</margin>
The book of the **Three Principles** <term>original: "drey Principiis"; Böhme’s system of the three worlds: the dark world (divine wrath/fire), the light world (divine love), and the external world (our visible nature).</term> of Divine Essence, and of the Essence of all Essences, is a key and an alphabet for all those who desire to understand my writings: and it deals with the Creation: with the **Eternal Birth** <term>original: "Ewige Gebuhrt"; the ongoing process by which God reveals Himself and generates the divine life.</term> of the Godhead: with Repentance, the Justification of man, and his life in Paradise, and with the Fall: Likewise, with the New Birth and Christ’s Testaments, and with the whole of human Salvation, etc., which is very profitable to read: For it is an eye to recognize the wonders in the **Mystery of God** <note>original: "Mysterio Gottes"; the hidden depths of the divine nature and the unfolding of His plan.</note>.

### Chapter 12. §. 15.

<margin>29.</margin>
The author’s description stands upon the ground of Scripture and is nothing new; nor will it ever become anything new, except for true knowledge in the **Holy Spirit** <note>original: "H. Geist"</note>, who is the Essence of all Essences.

<margin>30.</margin>
My writings are not written for the swine, who despise the **Light of Nature** <term>original: "Liecht der Natur"; a concept suggesting that God has placed a natural wisdom or "light" within the world that allows humans to understand spiritual truths through the physical creation.</term> and walk in animal ways: but for the children who are to possess the Kingdom of God. For I have written them for myself and for those who seek, and not for the clever and the wise of this world.
